title: Switch BSP server launch from interactive sbt + FIFO to `sbt -bsp`
body:
Follow-up to #186 / #187.

`scripts/development/start-sbt-metals.sh` currently launches the BSP server as a normal interactive `sbt` shell with BSP enabled, with a named FIFO bridging into stdin so the script can push `compile` (warm-up) and `exit` (clean shutdown). This works, but it is more machinery than the design calls for.

`sbt -bsp` is the official single-purpose BSP server mode. The known [sbt/sbt#6096](https://github.com/sbt/sbt/issues/6096) issue (sbtn hanging against `sbt -bsp` servers) was closed on 2020-11-16, so we should not be affected today.

## Switch

- Launch with `sbt -bsp -Dmicrotonalist.targetSuffix=-bsp`.
- Drop the FIFO and the `compile` warm-up — the user already runs `mcp__metals__compile-full` at session start, which warms the same JVM.
- Shutdown becomes a plain SIGTERM on the sbt PID (the script's existing trap already does that).
- Verify `sbtn` still routes correctly to a `sbt -bsp` server (target dir → `target-bsp/`, `logs/sbt.log` grows on each call). If `sbt -bsp` does not log task output into a file we control, log routing verification needs a different approach (e.g. inspecting the BSP server's own log location, or having the script tee `sbt -bsp`'s stderr to `logs/sbt.log`).

## Risk

The cleanup is small but it changes the script's IPC model. Land this on its own branch with full smoke testing before merging.
